question: Is passage-level triple co-occurrence (a local context subgraph) reliably available for the target facts in standard multi-hop KGQA datasets?
description: The mechanism requires that additional triples can be drawn 'from the same source passage' as the target triple/path. Passage-aligned KGs (text-derived) support this; curated KGs used in KGQA (e.g. Freebase-style) may not have per-triple provenance. Retrieval-augmented KGQA work (doi:10.20944/preprints202505.1992.v1, arxiv:2607.23278) suggests graph+text sources exist, but provenance granularity must be verified for the chosen dataset.
confidence_basis: Inferred from abstracts and the Freebase-based repo README; per-triple passage provenance was not explicitly stated or refuted in the sources read.
rationale: If provenance is absent, the operational definition of 'local context subgraph' must fall back to graph neighbourhood, changing what the method actually tests.
resolution: arxiv:2011.01060 (2WikiMultiHopQA) shows a dataset that combines structured (Wikidata) and unstructured data and attaches a reasoning path as evidence, and arxiv:2406.13397 builds on HotpotQA/2WikiMultihopQA/MuSiQue with sub-question-level reasoning annotations. Neither abstract states that individual triples carry a per-triple source-passage pointer, so passage-level triple co-occurrence is plausible for text-derived KGs but is not verified for the standard KGQA benchmarks (WebQSP/CWQ use Freebase in arxiv:2202.13296, with no passage notion). This means the operational definition of the 'local context subgraph' must be pinned to a specific dataset before the experiment, and a fallback to graph-neighbourhood context would collapse the idea into existing subgraph work.
